title: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism

solutions.title: One class per appointment type, one switch left at the factory
solutions.tradeoff: Three switch statements collapse into three small classes and a single factory switch, so knowing everything a checkup does now takes one file instead of three rows, but knowing everything about duration takes three files instead of one column - worth it only because the switch was genuinely repeated three times, and it would be over-engineering for one.

reviewFocus: Is there genuinely one switch left in the whole solution - the one inside createAppointment - or did a second one sneak back in inside a class method?
Does the walkthrough admit plainly that adding a fourth appointment type means touching every class file, rather than presenting polymorphism as a free win?
Would a lookup table of plain data have done this with less code, and does the walkthrough take an honest position on when that table would have been the better answer?
Do the three appointment classes share any logic that should have stayed a shared helper instead of being copied into each class?

Is createAppointment exhaustive without a default case, and does removing a case from AppointmentType actually fail the build the way the walkthrough claims - or is that asserted without being checked?
